_schema._about: Content for /work. Structure follows the reference customers page: a black carousel hero, a sand-s facts grid, a white quote wall, a white logo-grid block, then the full-bleed photo CTA. Every proof element on the reference is a reserved slot or an offer fact here (CONTRACT §10): hypjam has no clients and invents none. After those blocks comes hypjam's own formats wall (the concept tiles carried over from the existing /work page, disclosure kept). British English.
_schema.sections_order: The order the page agent should render: hero, facts, wall, platforms, formats, cta. (The task listed formats after the photo CTA; it is placed before so the full-bleed CTA closes the page as it does on the reference. Swap if the design lead prefers.)
_schema.hero: {h1, h1_break_after, sub_dim, controls:{prev, next}, cards:[{id, image:{kind, alt}, quote, attribution, meta, read:{label, inert}}]} - h1 wraps after h1_break_after on desktop, matching the reference's two-line heading; sub_dim sits under it at 40% opacity. The four cards keep the reference card anatomy exactly (image area 16:9, quote, attribution line, meta chip, 'Read' pill) but are reserved slots: dashed 1px sand-l/40 frame, a line-drawn phone silhouette in the image area (image.kind = phone-silhouette), and the strings given. 'Read' renders but is inert (no href, aria-disabled). This must look designed, not broken.
_schema.facts: {h2, p, animate, cells:[{value, suffix, label}]} - replaces the reference's 3x2 stats grid. Same numeral styling (display serif ~64px, sand-l) with the count-up from 0 when animate is true; the copy is commitments and offer facts, never results.
_schema.wall: {h2, p, cards:[{quote, name, role}]} - replaces the reference's quote wall. Kept minimal: three reserved cards in the same card style as the reference (sand-s tile, 18px serif quote, name, role), 'Filled in at launch' as the name and 'reserved' as the role.
_schema.platforms: {groups:[{label, tiles:[{id, text, render}]}]} - replaces the reference's logo grids. Group 1 is the row of five large tiles, group 2 the grid of smaller tiles. render = 'text' means the tile shows the name set typographically in Geist 500 at 60% opacity, monochrome (the same treatment as the hero marquee wordmarks). No third-party logo files.
_schema.formats: {eyebrow, h2, intro, formats:[{id, name, blurb, tags}], samples_label, samples:[{brand, format_id, hook, note, creator_brief, status}]} - hypjam's own formats wall. intro carries the honesty disclosure and must stay. samples are concept tiles: brand names are invented and disclosed as such; status is always 'illustrative' and renders as a small chip on every tile; creator_brief describes who we would cast rather than naming a handle.
_schema.cta: {h2, p, button:{label, href}, background:{kind, alt}} - the full-height photo CTA. We have no photography: background.kind = 'video-still' means the page agent uses a darkened blurred frame from the hero video (or a black-to-sand gradient if the video is missing).

formats.h2: UGC ads that sound like a creator, not a brand deck.
formats.intro: This is what ‘directed, not just sourced’ looks like on a feed: the formats we build, and sample tiles showing how a hook, a creator and a format come together. The brand names below are invented. We are new, and we would rather show the shape of the work than borrow someone else's logo.

formats.name: Hooks and ads
formats.blurb: The first three seconds decide everything, so that is where we spend most of our energy. We script, cast and shoot scroll-stopping hooks built for feed placement, not just brand safety.

formats.name: Testimonials
formats.blurb: Real people, real phones, real opinions, just aimed properly. We brief creators like actors, not customers, so the review still feels unscripted where it counts.

formats.name: Founder-led
formats.blurb: Sometimes the best spokesperson is the person who built the thing. We direct founders through the same process as the roster, hooks, retakes and all, so they do not have to wing it on camera.

formats.name: Trends and sounds
formats.blurb: We track what is actually moving on the app this week, not last quarter's trend report. Then we brief creators to bend it around your product instead of bolting your logo onto someone else's meme.

formats.name: Whitelisting
formats.blurb: Your best-performing organic content, running as paid from the creator's own handle. We handle the usage rights and the Spark Ads setup so the ad keeps the creator's credibility intact.

formats.name: Scripts and edits
formats.blurb: Every video starts as a proper script, not a vague vibe brief, and ends with an edit built for the platform it is going on. Same team end to end, so nothing gets lost in translation.
